#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
#
# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
#
#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
#
# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1

# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
else
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
fi

_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"

# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)

# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
_orch_not_implemented() {
    local fn_name="$1"
    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
    fi
    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
    return 1
}

# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.

if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
fi

# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
orch_has_capability() {
    local cap="$1"
    local caps
    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
_orch_find_backend_dir() {
    local alias="$1"
    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"

    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1

    local manifest plugin_dir
    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
        # Check provides.role
        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
            continue
        fi
        # Check id or provides.alias match
        local id declared_alias
        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
            echo "$plugin_dir"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)

    return 1
}

# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
# No fallback: a missing or unreadable backend is a hard misconfigured error.
orch_load_backend() {
    local backend="${1:-}"
    local plugin_dir

    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
                warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
                _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
                return 1
            fi
            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
        if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
            return 1
        fi
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # No plugin found and no fallback — hard misconfigured error naming the backend.
    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' not found — misconfigured (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias '${backend}')" || true
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions
# (i.e., when a plugin sources the backend before sourcing this contract file).
_orch_load_backend() {
    # If a real backend was already sourced (sentinel set to 1), skip auto-load
    # to avoid overwriting the pre-loaded backend's implementations.
    # Note: the stubs above do NOT set this sentinel, so checking declare -F
    # would always return true (stubs are defined).  We use the sentinel instead.
    [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -eq 1 ]] && return 0

    local backend

    # Get configured backend, falling back to "sequential" if config unavailable
    if declare -F zbuild_config_get_backend >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        backend="$(zbuild_config_get_backend "orchestrator" 2>/dev/null)" || backend="sequential"
    else
        backend="${ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND:-sequential}"
    fi

    # Attempt to load the configured backend; if it fails, that is OK —
    # the stubs remain and callers will get informative errors.
    orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Auto-load at source time — skipped if _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is already 1
_orch_load_backend

310	        diverged)

312	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true

318	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
319	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
320	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
321	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
322	# never blocks a run.
323	#
324	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
325	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
326	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
327	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
328	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
329	# item 1 of #1807.
330	#
331	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
332	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
333	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
334	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
335	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
336	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
337	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
338	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
339	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
340	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
341	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
342	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
343	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
344	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
345	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
346	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
347	    # push had nothing to send.
348	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
349	
350	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
351	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
352	        saved)
353	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
354	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
355	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
356	            ;;
357	        failed)
358	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
359	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
360	            # no channel to surface on.
361	            #
362	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
363	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
364	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
365	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
366	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
367	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
368	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
369	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
370	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
371	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
372	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
373	            fi
374	            ;;
375	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
376	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
377	        *) : ;;
378	    esac
379	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
380	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
381	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
382	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
383	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
384	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
385	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
386	    local _leak=""
387	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
388	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
389	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
390	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
391	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
392	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
393	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
394	        return 0
395	    fi
396	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
397	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
398	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
399	    fi
400	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
401	    return 0
402	}

404	# ─── stage-start time cache (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────
405	# Populated immediately before _render_stage_divider for each stage; read at
406	# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
407	# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.
408	declare -gA _RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS=()

410	# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
411	# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
412	# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
413	# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty
414	# until set; readers degrade to "?s" on cache-miss (mirrors _runner_duration_token).
415	_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS=""

417	# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
418	# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
419	# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
420	# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
421	# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
422	# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
423	_runner_now_ms() {
424	    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
425	    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
426	        printf '%s' "$ovr"
427	        return 0
428	    fi
429	    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
430	        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
431	        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
432	        return 0
433	    fi
434	    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"
435	}

437	# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
438	# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
439	# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
440	# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
441	# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
442	# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
443	# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
444	# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
445	# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
446	_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
447	_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
448	    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
449	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
450	    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
451	    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
452	    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
453	    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
454	    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
455	    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
456	    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
457	    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
458	    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
459	    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
460	    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
461	    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
462	      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
463	           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
464	           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
465	        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
466	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
467	    return 0
468	}

470	# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
471	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
472	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
473	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
474	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
475	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
476	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
477	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
478	    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
479	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
480	        local i
481	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
482	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
483	            sleep 0.1
484	        done
485	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
486	    fi
487	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
488	    return 0
489	}

491	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
492	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
493	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
494	_runner_now_short() {
495	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
496	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
497	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
498	        return 0
499	    fi
500	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
501	    local out
502	    # The shell's clock, in UTC (ADR-065 §5); the date forms stay as the fallback.
503	    TZ=UTC printf -v out '%(%H:%M:%S UTC)T' "$sec" 2>/dev/null && [[ -n "$out" ]] && { printf '%s' "$out"; return 0; }
504	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
505	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
506	        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
507	    printf '%s' "$out"
508	}

510	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
511	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
512	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
513	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
514	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
515	_runner_duration_token() {
516	    local stage="$1"
517	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
518	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
519	        printf '?s'
520	        return 0
521	    fi
522	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
523	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
524	        printf '?s'
525	        return 0
526	    fi
527	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
528	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
529	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
530	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
531	    else
532	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
533	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
534	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
535	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
536	    fi
537	}

539	# ─── _runner_export_scope_allowlist <state_dir> (ADR-043) ────────────────────
540	# Redaction by construction: the per-run scope allowlist, exported as
541	# ZBUILD_SCOPE_ALLOWLIST so route_to_model can redact without a plugin passing
542	# it. Called per-stage because nothing is reported before plan runs (empty then —
543	# harmless, the scope manifest is the base allowlist and this is purely ADDITIVE).
544	_runner_export_scope_allowlist() {
545	    local state_dir="$1"
546	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" csv=""
547	    # #2189: the scope files stages REPORTED (plan reports its files) — the
548	    # engine no longer reads plan.json by path.
549	    if [[ -s "$rec" ]]; then
550	        csv="$(jq -r '(.scope_files // []) | unique | join(",")' "$rec" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
551	    fi
552	    # #1874: the shape floor is part of the scope — computed here, mechanically,
553	    # so build, redaction and shape-floor all read one list that already holds
554	    # the files a shape change owes. Memoised per scope: this runs every stage.
555	    if [[ -n "$csv" && "$csv" != "${_RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY:-}" ]]; then
556	        _RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY="$csv"; _RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV="$csv"
557	        if ! declare -F sf_scope_floor_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
558	            # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/shape-floor.sh
559	            source "${_ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib}/shape-floor.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
560	        fi
561	        if declare -F sf_scope_floor_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
562	            local -a _scope_arr=() ; local _ff
563	            IFS=',' read -r -a _scope_arr <<< "$csv"
564	            while IFS= read -r _ff; do
565	                [[ -n "$_ff" && ",$_RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV," != *",$_ff,"* ]] && _RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV+=",$_ff"
566	            done < <(sf_scope_floor_files "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" "${_scope_arr[@]}" 2>/dev/null)
567	        fi
568	    fi
569	    [[ -n "$csv" ]] && csv="${_RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV:-$csv}"

573	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
574	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
575	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
576	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
577	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
578	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
579	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
580	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
581	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
582	_runner_record_report() {
583	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
584	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
585	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
586	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
587	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
588	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
589	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
590	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
591	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
592	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
593	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
594	        sleep 0.05
595	    done
596	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
597	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
598	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
599	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
600	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
601	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
602	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
603	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
604	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
605	    else
606	        rm -f "$tmp"
607	    fi
608	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
609	    return 0
610	}

612	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
613	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
614	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
615	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
616	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
617	#
618	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
619	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
620	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
621	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
622	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
623	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
624	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
625	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
626	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
627	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
628	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
629	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
630	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
631	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
632	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
633	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
634	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
635	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
636	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
637	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
638	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
639	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
640	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
641	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
642	        return 1
643	    fi
644	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
645	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
646	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
647	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
648	        return 1
649	    fi
650	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
651	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
652	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
653	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
654	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
655	    #
656	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
657	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
658	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
659	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
660	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
661	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
662	    #
663	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
664	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
665	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
666	    #
667	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
668	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
669	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
670	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
671	    fi
672	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
673	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
674	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
675	    # an unchanged tree.
676	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
677	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
678	    fi
679	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
680	    local _leaf _ok=1
681	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
682	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
683	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
684	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
685	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
686	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
687	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
688	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
689	        esac
690	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
691	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
692	            _ok=0
693	        fi
694	    done
695	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
696	}

698	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
699	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
700	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
701	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
702	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
703	#
704	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
705	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
706	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
707	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
708	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
709	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
710	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
711	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
712	#
713	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
714	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
715	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
716	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
717	#
718	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
719	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
720	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
721	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
722	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
723	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
724	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
725	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
726	_runner_template_personas() {
727	    awk '
728	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
729	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }

928	_render_pipeline_end() {

931	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
932	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"

937	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
938	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
939	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
940	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
941	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
942	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
943	    # (#1156)

951	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload

956	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
957	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
958	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
959	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
960	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
961	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;

965	    local label=" pipeline.end "

968	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))

981	        {

983	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"

985	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \

990	    fi

992	    local lbar rbar

994	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
995	    {

997	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
998	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
999	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"

1001	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
1002	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"

1022	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1023	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1024	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it

1030	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1031	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1032	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1033	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1034	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1

1054	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2

1056	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''

1061	            printf '\n'

1063	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.

1090	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1091	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1092	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1093	#
1094	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1095	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)

1124	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1125	    {
1126	        printf '\n'

1128	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1129	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"

1163	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1164	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1165	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering parallel group: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1166	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1167	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$group_id" "${RESET:-}"
1168	        printf '%b  (max_parallel=%s · members=%s)%b\n' \
1169	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$members_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1170	        printf '\n'
1171	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1172	}
1173	
1174	# ─── _render_parallel_group_complete <group_id> <member_count> <failure_count> ─
1175	# Issue OUT (ADR-039): DIM trailer after a parallel group's per-member lines,
1176	# mirroring _render_cycle_exit's role for cycles. e.g.
1177	# `▸ review_lenses complete — 5 members, 0 blocking`.
1178	_render_parallel_group_complete() {
1179	    local group_id="$1" count="${2:-0}" fail="${3:-0}"
1180	    {
1181	        printf '%b▸ %s complete — %s members, %s blocking%b\n' \
1182	            "${DIM:-}" "$group_id" "$count" "$fail" "${RESET:-}"
1183	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1184	}
1185	
1186	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_divider <cycle_id> <iter> <max> ───────────────────────
1187	# Light `─` CYAN sub-divider for each iter boundary, e.g.
1188	# `─── build_test_cycle iter 2/5 ─────`. When this cycle is nested inside
1189	# another cycle the orchestrator has already set ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX (e.g.
1190	# `4.1`) — surface it as a `[<prefix>]` prefix so operators can tell at a
1191	# glance which outer iter this divider belongs to:
1192	#   outer (no prefix): `─── build_review_cycle iter 1/2 ───`
1193	#   inner (prefix set): `─── [4.1] build_test_cycle iter 1/3 ───`
1194	# Reuses the seq-prefix machinery from Wave 19-B #718 / cycle-orchestrator.sh:888
1195	# — no new plumbing, no hook-signature change. Emitted by the orchestrator's
1196	# iter-begin hook BEFORE the first per-stage banner of the iter.
1197	_render_cycle_iter_divider() {
1198	    local cycle_id="$1" iter="$2" max="$3"
1199	    local prefix="${ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX:-}"
1200	    local label
1201	    if [[ -n "$prefix" ]]; then
1202	        label=" [${prefix}] ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1203	    else
1204	        label=" ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1205	    fi
1206	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1207	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1208	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1209	    local bar
1210	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1211	    bar="${bar// /─}"
1212	    {
1213	        printf '\n%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1214	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1215	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1216	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1217	}
1218	
1219	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_complete <iter> <verdict> <score> <fc> <elapsed_s> ──
1220	# Per-iter DIM trailer line e.g. `↳ iter 2 complete: verdict=pass score=-1
1221	# failure_count=1 elapsed=4s`. Emitted by the orchestrator's iter-complete
1222	# hook AFTER the `cycle.iteration.complete` event is durable. #1254: the
1223	# `score` axis (progress − defects) replaced the retired `velocity` label so
1224	# the per-iter line matches the OUTPUT banner's health score.
1225	_render_cycle_iter_complete() {
1226	    local iter="$1" verdict="$2" score="$3" failure_count="$4" elapsed_s="$5"
1227	    {
1228	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1229	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1230	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
